 Judgment

Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 01.07.2019 passed by the Senior Civil Judge & MACT at Kadur, Chikkamagalur Disitrct (for short 'the Tribunal'), in MVC No.39/2016, the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge & MACT at Kadur, Chikkamagalur Disitrct
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
That on 03.06.2015 at about 10.30 a.m., the petitioner was riding the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA.18/K-8568 and he met with an accident near Seegehadlu - Kamanagere road with a lorry bearing registration No.KA.21/E-9989, which was duly insured with the third respondent.
The accident is said to have happened due to rash and negligent driving of the offending lorry.

The petitioner sustained the following injuries:-
a. Type III comminuted intercondylar.
b. Fracture of left humerus.
c. Multiple abrasion over left arm.
d. Multiple abrasion on left frontal region.
e. Abrasion over left shoulder.
f. Suture wound over left elbow.
g. Deformity at left elbow.
h. Swelling over left elbow.

4. The Tribunal, based on the evidence let in, has awarded a compensation of Rs.2,25,696/- along with interest @ 7% p.a. under the following heads:-

5.
Not satisfied by the same, the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.
6. The accident happened in the year 2015.
The petitioner was aged 24 years.
His income has not been established before the Tribunal.
Hence, the notional income as prescribed in the Lok-Adalath chart has to be considered which will be Rs.9,000/- per month.
The Tribunal has taken the disability at 8% to the whole body and has granted a sum of Rs.1,03,680/- towards 'future loss of income'.
The petitioner was aged 24 years at the time of accident.
Hence, the multiplier of '18' has to be adopted as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma & Ors vs Delhi Transport Corp.& Anr reported in 2009(6) SCC 121.

entities.text: Sarla Verma & Ors vs Delhi Transport Corp.& Anr reported in 2009(6) SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, towards 'future loss of income', the petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.1,55,520/-(9000x12x18x8%).
Towards 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/-.
I deem the same to be appropriate.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.38,416/-
towards 'medical expenses'.
As the same is based on the actual bills submitted by the petitioner, the same is retained.
Towards 'conveyance charges', the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/-.
I deem the same to be appropriate.
Towards ' food nourishment and attendant charges', the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/-.
I deem the same to be appropriate.

Given the nature of injuries,
the laid up period has to be considered atleast 3 months and a sum of Rs.27,000/-
(9000x3=27,000/-) is awarded under this head.
The Tribunal has not awarded any compensation towards 'loss of amenities'.
Given the nature of injuries, I deem it appropriate to award a sum of Rs.40,000/- under this head.
7. Thus, the compensation to the petitioner under different heads is modified as hereunder:-

Thus, the petitioner is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,15,240/-(Rs.3,40,936/- -
Rs.2,25,696/-).

Hence, the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is partly allowed;
ii) The total compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified and petitioner is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,15,240/-(Rupees One Lakh Fifteen Thousand Two Hundred and Forty only) over and above what has been already awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition before the Tribunal till the date of realization.
iii) Respondent No.3 - Insurance Company shall pay the enhanced compensation to the petitioner along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of the certified copy of the judgment and order.
iv) Draw modified award accordingly.
